cards.title: Revision River Ferry Ending Switch
cards.cardSkill: Revise a shared table idea by choosing the clearest ending detail.
cards.tableFit: Upper-age cooperative family-table card for a calm paper-and-pencil story round.
cards.adultSetup: Set one printed card near the pencils and ask the table to choose one ferry detail everyone may borrow.
cards.kidDirection: Draft a river scene, revise one sentence, and choose an ending that echoes an earlier clue.
cards.hostPrompt: Ask which detail should return at the dock and which extra sentence can be trimmed.

pageSections.heading: Ferry Start
lines: The ferry carries a small object shaped like ____________________.
The river setting feels ____________________ because of one detail.
The table clue everyone may borrow is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Revision Turn
lines: My first ending idea is ____________________.
One sentence I can make clearer is ____________________.
The detail that should return near the dock is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Dock Ending
lines: The ferry reaches the dock when ____________________.
My revised final image is ____________________.
The ending choice I like best is ____________________.

cards.tableTalkLine: Tell the table one detail you kept after revising: ____________________.
cards.tinyDraftLine: Tiny draft: The ferry changed course when ____________________.
cards.roundWrapLine: This round made my ending clearer by ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: circle one sentence to revise and copy it here: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeStoryLine: Take-home story starter: A ferry ticket with a revised note says ____________________.

cards.title: Clue Label Tower Sensory Case
cards.cardSkill: Select precise setting details and turn them into a concise story label.
cards.tableFit: Upper-age cooperative family-table card for screen-free observation, sorting, and short writing.
cards.adultSetup: Place the card in the center and invite the table to name one quiet museum case, shelf, or tower detail.
cards.kidDirection: Choose one clue, add a sensory detail, and write a label that points a reader into the scene.
cards.hostPrompt: Ask which clue belongs in the first sentence and which detail is only background.

pageSections.heading: Case Clues
lines: The tower case holds something that looks like ____________________.
A sound, texture, or color near it is ____________________.
The clue the table can reuse is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Label Focus
lines: The label should help readers notice ____________________.
The detail I will leave in the background is ____________________.
The strongest setting word on my card is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Museum Scene
lines: My story label begins with ____________________.
The scene changes when someone notices ____________________.
The label makes the setting feel ____________________.

cards.tableTalkLine: Share one setting word the table could borrow: ____________________.
cards.tinyDraftLine: Tiny draft: The tower label pointed toward ____________________.
cards.roundWrapLine: This round helped me choose the clearest clue: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: write only your final invented label here: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeStoryLine: Take-home story starter: A label on an ordinary shelf explains ____________________.

cards.title: Compass Craft Academy Route Choice
cards.cardSkill: Build sequence with a clear route, character choice, and turning point.
cards.tableFit: Upper-age cooperative family-table card for mapping a short scene with three connected steps.
cards.adultSetup: Invite the table to agree on one starting place, one turn, and one finish before anyone writes.
cards.kidDirection: Plan a three-stop route, choose what the main character decides, and draft the turning sentence.
cards.hostPrompt: Ask which stop changes the plan and which map word helps readers follow the sequence.

pageSections.heading: Route Map
lines: The route starts beside ____________________.
The middle stop reveals ____________________.
The finish point waits near ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Choice Point
lines: The main character chooses to ____________________.
The reason for that choice is ____________________.
A compass word that shows the next step is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Sequence Draft
lines: First, the route moves through ____________________.
Next, the plan changes because ____________________.
Finally, the ending lands at ____________________.

cards.tableTalkLine: Tell the table which stop changed the route: ____________________.
cards.tinyDraftLine: Tiny draft: The compass pointed next to ____________________.
cards.roundWrapLine: This round made my sequence clearer by ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: draw three route dots and write the middle turn: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeStoryLine: Take-home story starter: A hallway map at home leads from ____________________ to ____________________.

cards.title: Almost Invention Workshop Test Note
cards.cardSkill: Use ordered steps, sensory detail, and revision to explain a paper invention.
cards.tableFit: Upper-age cooperative family-table card for inventing a simple paper-only idea together.
cards.adultSetup: Ask the table to pick one simple household problem for an imaginary paper tool to help explain.
cards.kidDirection: Invent a nearly useful paper tool, write three ordered steps, and revise one test note.
cards.hostPrompt: Ask where the directions need a clearer verb, label, or sensory detail.

pageSections.heading: Workshop Idea
lines: The paper-only invention is called ____________________.
It is meant to help with ____________________.
The texture, color, or shape detail is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Step Order
lines: Step one tells the reader to ____________________.
Step two changes the tool by ____________________.
Step three checks whether ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Test Note
lines: The part that almost works is ____________________.
The direction I should revise is ____________________.
The final test note says ____________________.

cards.tableTalkLine: Share one verb that made the directions clearer: ____________________.
cards.tinyDraftLine: Tiny draft: The almost-invention worked better after ____________________.
cards.roundWrapLine: This round helped me revise the step that says ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: revise one direction silently and write it here: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeStoryLine: Take-home story starter: A paper tool on the kitchen table almost solves ____________________.

cards.title: Index Card Theater Dialogue Turn
cards.cardSkill: Write concise dialogue that reveals character choice and ending direction.
cards.tableFit: Upper-age cooperative family-table card for a short two-voice scene on printable cards.
cards.adultSetup: Invite the table to choose one setting cue and one shared object before writers draft two spoken lines.
cards.kidDirection: Write two lines of dialogue, show what a character chooses, and end with a clear scene shift.
cards.hostPrompt: Ask what the first line expects and how the reply changes the scene direction.
